problem: Prior navigation policies (transformer- and diffusion-based, e.g. NoMaD) need external planners, manual mode switching or task-specific supervision to balance exploration and goal-directed navigation. Prior active-inference (AIF) navigation work is mostly simulated, and usually covers only epistemic or only extrinsic value.
motivation: In real environments, perceptual aliasing (e.g. similar chairs along walls) makes localization from the current observation ambiguous, so a robot must explore to reduce uncertainty before heading to the goal. AIF's expected free energy (EFE) unifies both behaviors in one objective, but scaling it needs diverse action proposals and reliable long-horizon prediction, which deep generative models could provide.
key_idea: Use a diffusion policy as a learned action prior to sample candidate action sequences, imagine each with a multiple-timescale RSSM (MTRSSM) world model, and pick the sequence with the lowest EFE (epistemic KL + goal-feature-distance extrinsic term).
insight: Exploration and goal-seeking emerge from one EFE criterion. Only Extrinsic drops to 28% success in exploration-demanding cases versus 78% for the full method. Replacing MTRSSM with RSSM lowers success from 75% to 64%. Replacing the diffusion policy with a Gaussian sampler gives 36.1%, and CEM gives 0% success. Table 2 shows MTRSSM has better 200-step imagination (LPIPS 0.204 vs 0.277) with fewer parameters than RSSM and even a larger RSSM. Its higher-level states form a closed loop that encodes the room structure.
method: Diffusion policy: 1D-UNet with DDIM, conditioned on the two latest observations via CNN + spatial softmax. It generates T_F=64-step velocity sequences (K=10 at test time, 8 candidates) and executes the first T_a=32 steps; it is treated as a data-driven prior P0(a|o).
MTRSSM world model: two-level RSSM with MTRNN deterministic states (tau_h=64, tau_l=4) and categorical stochastic states, trained with a VFE-style loss. It provides long-horizon latent imagination.

EFE evaluation by latent imagination: for each candidate, sample M=5 high-level and N=5 low-level latents per step, decode imagined observations, and re-infer the posterior. Epistemic value is the low-level KL(posterior||prior).
Extrinsic value: feature-space MSE between imagined observations and the goal image, using a CNN encoder trained so feature distance reflects spatial distance from odometry.

Precision schedule: a sigmoid over inference iterations (0.08 to 3.0) makes the epistemic term dominate early and the extrinsic term late. The lowest-EFE sequence is executed (sampling-based policy inference P ∝ P0·exp(-G)).

setting.backbone: Diffusion policy (1D-UNet) + MTRSSM (~165k params), both trained from scratch
setting.training_data: 30,000 steps (15 sequences x 2,000 at 5 Hz) of teleoperated roaming RGB + velocity in one indoor room, no goal labels
setting.observation: monocular wide-angle RGB (240x320; downsampled to 120x160 for the policy and 60x80 for the world model) plus a goal image
setting.action_space: continuous linear and angular velocity commands (TurtleBot 4)
setting.privileged: none at test time (goal image only); the NoMaD/FlowNav baselines were given topological maps built from expert trajectories

numbers_note: Only a custom single-room real-robot benchmark is reported; there are no standard benchmarks and no SPL. Baselines: Only Extrinsic 53% SR, FlowNav 50%, NoMaD 8.33%. Ablations: RSSM 64%, GSP 36.1%, CEM 0% (9 trials).
results: On 36 real-robot trials the method reaches 75% SR with 0.806 collisions per trial, beating Only Extrinsic (53%), FlowNav (50%) and NoMaD (8.33%), even though the latter two were given expert topological maps. The gain is largest in exploration-demanding cases (78% vs 28% for Only Extrinsic). Success falls to 69.4% with random starts and goals and to 37.5% with unseen obstacles.
limitations: Tested in a single 4.7x6.3 m room; performance drops sharply with unseen visual changes (37.5%).
Slow inference (~5 s per decision) because of EFE computation over candidates; long-horizon imagination still fails at times.
Extrinsic precision is a hand-tuned schedule, and the goal-proximity feature encoder is unreliable under aliasing.
